lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: Are poor people poor because they make bad decisions? Possibly. Although in America, a bank can charge you thirty-five dollars for not having enough money.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: The case for decisions is real. Finish school, work full time, marry before kids. Of households that did all three, about two percent were poor.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: But correlation isn't cause. In one marshmallow test, kids who'd just been let down by an adult waited three minutes. Kids whose adult kept a promise waited twelve.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: Scarcity also eats brainpower. Indian sugarcane farmers did worse on reasoning tests before harvest, when money was tight, than after it.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: And being poor is expensive. A typical payday loan works out at almost four hundred percent a year. Good boots cost more up front. Cheap boots cost more in the end.

lines.speaker: benny
lines.text: Money's cheaper if you've already got some.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: Place matters too. Kids whose families won a lottery to move somewhere less poor before age thirteen earned thirty-one percent more as young adults.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: Choices matter. But they're made on a very uneven board. And when a poor person makes a mistake, it comes with a late fee.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: So the real question isn't whether poor people make bad decisions. Everyone does. It's why theirs cost so much more. Full video on our channel.
